title: Cross-language pagination & batch-iterator: unified ergonomics for embeddings and rerank
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Problem: Each SDK has evolved slightly different idioms for paginating embeddings/rerank results and batching requests. Python uses async iterators, TypeScript provides Promise-based streaming helpers, and Go exposes channel-style streaming. This inconsistency makes cross-platform examples and reference apps confusing and increases maintenance burden.

Goal: Design and implement a small, well-documented set of helpers that provide: 1) a uniform pagination cursor abstraction for list endpoints (e.g., /embeddings/list, /rerank/queries), 2) a batch iterator that yields request batches tuned for throughput/latency tradeoffs, and 3) ergonomic streaming collectors for partial rerank / embeddings responses. The APIs should feel idiomatic per language while mapping to the same conceptual primitives so examples and docs can be shared.

Scope: Implement helpers in Python, TypeScript, and Go; update docs and add cross-language end-to-end examples for batching + pagination combined with retry/backoff policies and streaming aggregation. Backwards compatibility is required: all new helpers should be additive and opt-in.

Design highlights and API sketches (high level):
- Core concepts: Cursor (opaque string), Pager (high-level enumerator that returns items across pages), BatchCursor (groups N items into request batches), RetryPolicy (config for retries + jitter), StreamCollector (aggregates partial streams into final typed result).
- Python: async iterator pattern (class VectorPager: async for vec in pager: ...) and BatchCursor.async_batches(batch_size=256). RetryPolicy integrates with existing httpx transport used by SDK.
- TypeScript: async generator functions (for await (const v of pager())) and a BatchBuilder that returns arrays of items; Node SDK will expose backpressure hint via optional signal/throughput param.
- Go: channel-based iterators (Pager(ctx) -> <-chan Item) and BatchIterator(ctx, batchSize) -> chan []Item. Go retry hooks integrate with context for cancellations.

Non-goals: Rewriting existing streaming primitives, changing public method names for current stable API, or enforcing one single runtime representation across languages. This is additive ergonomic sugar to improve parity and docs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New helpers implemented in python, ts, go SDKs with consistent README examples; 2) Cross-lang example app demonstrating paginated list -> batch -> multi-request rerank pipeline; 3) Unit tests covering cursor boundaries, empty pages, and retry/backoff behavior; 4) Performance regression: <5% overhead vs hand-rolled batching in integration test; 5) Documentation and snippets added to sdk/README and quickstart; 6) API review signoff from SDK leads in PRs.

implementation_notes:
Python: expose async class VectorPager(client, endpoint, page_size=1000, dedupe='keep_first', max_bytes=None) and BatchCursor.async_batches(batch_size=256, max_bytes=None). TypeScript: export function pager(client, opts): AsyncGenerator<Item> and export function batchBuilder(opts): AsyncIterable<Array<Item>>. Go: Pager(ctx, client, opts) returns (<-chan Item, <-chan error). RetryPolicy implemented as a small transport wrapper to minimize per-language duplication.

Tradeoffs and decisions:
- We keep cursors opaque to clients to allow server-side cursor format changes.
- Default batch sizes tuned conservatively (256 vectors) to avoid timeouts on shared hosted tier. Customers on Dedicated can increase.
- Retry defaults are conservative to avoid double-processing side-effects for rerank endpoints; we expose a flag to opt-in to more aggressive retrying when callers assert idempotency.

Next steps:

- Run cross-language perf suite on dedicated GPU cluster (scheduled 2026-03-10).

notes_for_reviewers: Please review the language idioms in the PRs rather than line-by-line parity. The goal is conceptual parity with idiomatic surface. Key checks: cancellation behavior, de-duplication semantics, default retry settings, and memory safety for streaming collectors. Refer to the Confluence doc for rationales and benchmarks.
